resources.name: map_layer_cell_heatmap_description
resources.value: Your observed cellular landscape by radio technology. Soft fields show where serving cells reached you; glowing centers are conservative site estimates and become sharper only when observations surround them.

resources.name: map_layer_distinct_visits_description
resources.value: Relative density of accepted location fixes. This shows distinct observations, not time spent.

resources.name: map_layer_signal_coverage_description
resources.value: Highlights where your cell signal was weak or missing. The redder the area, the worse the coverage; well-covered areas stay clear.

resources.name: map_layer_signal_aurora_description
resources.value: Cell signal rendered as an aurora-like glow: a broad violet halo beneath a bright cyan-green core. The glow breathes without reloading data and becomes static when system animations are disabled.

resources.name: map_layer_speed_heatmap_description
resources.value: Heatmap representing the speed of movement across different areas.

resources.name: map_layer_legacy_heatmap_description
resources.value: Throwback to the original Signals app: your location density drawn as discrete 25\u202fm grid tiles, the way the heatmap looked when tiles were rendered on the server. Zoom in to see the squares.

resources.name: map_layer_seasonal_description
resources.value: A patchwork of seasonal memory: every area you\u2019ve explored is tinted by the season you first visited it in. Find the trails you only ever walk in summer, or the streets you only see in winter.

resources.name: map_layer_terrain_description
resources.value: Your location density lifted into 3D: the places you spend the most time rise as tall glowing mesas, while one-off spots stay low. Tilt the map to see the relief of your life.

resources.name: map_layer_places_description
resources.value: Your important places as markers, each sized and coloured by how often you visit. Home and work become big warm dots; a place you went once stays a small cool one.

resources.name: map_layer_speed_ribbon_description
resources.value: Your route painted by how fast you were moving, flowing colour from a slow violet amble to a red-hot sprint or drive. Unlike the speed heatmap, the ribbon keeps your path intact so you can see exactly where you sped up and slowed down.

resources.name: map_layer_altitude_ribbon_description
resources.value: Your route painted by absolute elevation, from deep blue lowlands through cyan foothills to warm mountain heights. The scale stays fixed as you pan, so the same altitude always keeps the same colour.

resources.name: map_layer_activity_ribbon_description
resources.value: Your route painted by the reliable motion state recorded with each fix: grey where state was unknown, blue while still, and green while moving.

resources.name: map_layer_ski_xray_description
resources.value: A diagnostic view of detected ski segments. Downhill runs, lifts, walks, and pauses are anchored to the nearest recorded location and labelled with their key metrics.

resources.name: map_layer_trip_constellations_description
resources.value: Repeated journeys between your frequent places become curved constellations. A stable arc shows each route while a comet travels along it; thicker arcs mean you made that journey more often.

resources.name: map_layer_fog_description
resources.value: The world emerging from the fog: every area you\u2019ve touched is revealed, glowing brighter the more thoroughly you got to know it. Places you merely passed through stay a faint haze; somewhere you explored deeply burns solid gold. Unexplored ground stays dark.

resources.name: map_layer_first_contact_description
resources.value: A timeline of your discoveries: each area is coloured by how recently you first set foot there. The places you found long ago fade to deep indigo, while ground you broke this week glows bright cyan\u2014read the story of your exploration outward to your newest frontiers.

resources.name: map_layer_vehicle_compliance_description
resources.value: Polyline of driving samples coloured by how the speed compares to your configured baseline limit.

resources.name: map_layer_location_polyline_description
resources.value: Line connecting your recorded locations over time.

resources.name: map_layer_wifi_count_heatmap_description
resources.value: Shows how many distinct access points overlap at each place. Repeated scans of the same AP count once, so hotter areas mean genuinely denser radio coverage.

resources.name: map_layer_wifi_heatmap_description
resources.value: A band-aware Wi-Fi constellation from your own observations. Colored fields show observed 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz coverage; glowing centers are approximate AP positions shown only when the sample geometry supports them.
